## Choosing the right template in the FIP Wizard

Project templates in the FIP Wizard are based on Knowledge Models. 

There are four main blocks of templates:

### Creating FAIR Supporting Resource descriptions

- Creating a description from scratch: choose **FAIR Supporting Resource**:
This template works for both FAIR Supporting Resources and for FAIR Enablig Resources. In case you used this template for describing a resource but discover only at a later stage that you want to link it to a FAIRsharing record, you can still add this link in the field: Related metadata to which this metadata can be mapped. 

- Creating a FAIR Supporting Resource metadata record based on FAIRsharing description:  choose **FSR based on FAIRsharing**
This template allows you to reuse a FAIRsharing record for prefilling the description field and access links as a starting point. 

### Creating FAIR Implementation Profiles (FIP)

- Creating a FIP focusing on essential FAIR Enabling Resource related questions: choose **FAIR Implementation Profile basic**
This template includes a total of 21 questions. Most of these questions are already pre-answered with "No implementation choice" which can be easily revoked. 

- Creating a FIP including questions beyond FAIR Enabling Resources: choose **FAIR Implementation Profile extended**
This template includes questions for FAIR Supporting Resources like validations services or editors adding up to 39 questions in total. Most of these questions are already pre-answered with "No implementation choice" which can be easily revoked. 

- Creating a FIP that functions as a reference for your community members: choose **R-FIP**
This template includes questions related to all FAIR Supporting Resource Types. 

### Creating additional FIP related concepts:

- Creating a description of your community: choose **FAIR Implementation Community*
This template is needed to be used to provide a description about your community that wants to publish a FIP.

- Creating a new concept for digital object type: choose **New FIP-related term** (subject to change)
Use this template and choose **digital object type** to define a new type not listed in the drop-down. 

### Creating requirements related descriptions:

- Creating a description of the case study: choose **Case Study Description**

- Creating a description of your user story: choose **User Story**

- For analysing a representative digital object: choose **Digital Object Analysis*+
